correctness.rationale: The Gaussian potential is locally integrable, its integration-by-parts ODE and Dawson solution are checked. The crossing t*w(t)=1 exists uniquely because w>0, w~1/t and every level-one crossing has positive derivative. Thus F_a(s) has one global minimum. Correct limits establish the two-root trichotomy. SLLN and LIL give exact almost-sure and boundary behavior; positive Gaussian density at the denominator pole gives all p>=1 moments infinite. Fractional moments follow from integrability and Jensen. The 824-check standalone verifier was executed; finite checks do not certify asymptotic facts.

value.rationale: The precise, universal scaled-drift cutoff and two noise thresholds locate a nonmonotone stability hazard for implicit time-stepping with unbounded uncertainty in the implicit operator. The rigorous separation of almost-sure contraction from every first and higher moment is an informative numerical-reliability boundary. It is not a routine renaming of a known method: the noncentral Gaussian logarithmic-potential minimization and its unique crossing are the substantive steps.
